### **1. Given Data**
- Voltage ($V$) = $240\text{ V}$
- Real Power ($P$) = $2\text{ kW} = 2000\text{ W}$
- Power Factor ($\cos\phi$) = $0.6$ (lagging)

### **2. Calculate Current ($I$)**
$$P = V \cdot I \cdot \cos\phi$$
$$2000 = 240 \cdot I \cdot 0.6$$
$$I = \frac{2000}{144} = 13.89\text{ A}$$.

### **3. Calculate Apparent Power ($	ext{kVA}$)**
$$\text{Apparent Power} = V \cdot I = 240 \times 13.89 = 3333.33\text{ VA} = 3.333\text{ kVA}$$.

### **4. Calculate Reactive Power ($	ext{kVAr}$)**
$$\text{Power Factor angle } \phi = \arccos(0.6) = 53.13^\circ$$
$$\text{Reactive Power} = V \cdot I \cdot \sin\phi = 3333.33 \times \sin(53.13^\circ) = 3333.33 \times 0.8 = 2666.67\text{ VAr} = 2.667\text{ kVAr}$$.
proTip: You can also find reactive power directly using the relation $Q = \sqrt{S^2 - P^2} = \sqrt{3.333^2 - 2^2} = 2.667\text{ kVAr}$.
